svg.title: Programming a PIM + VPU accelerator
svg.desc: The host stages an add job in lane 3. Its DarkRISCV core sends IADDR to private RAM and receives a 32-bit instruction on IDATA one clock later. Eight scalar lanes run one program on strided pairs of global indices. Lane 3 adds the residual at indices 3 and 11, returning 10 and 18. Lab 5 runs PIM, host scaling and VPU jobs in sequence. An integrated, double-buffered design could project block B as the VPU consumes the scaled result of block A.

g.inkscape:label: Page and title
g.text: The PIM arrays compute the matrix projection. Eight scalar RISC-V lanes add the residual.

g.inkscape:label: A · Instruction fetch and job dispatch

text.tspan: Each lane gets the same firmware. The host sets ADD, count = 2 and done = 0, releases lane 3 from reset,
then reads both sums when done = 1.

g.inkscape:label: B · Eight-lane vector assignment
g.text: How eight lanes divide a 16-element vector
Single program, multiple data (SPMD). Each core has its own program counter and runs the scalar add loop over two elements.

g.inkscape:label: C · Sequential and overlapped schedules
g.text: When can PIM and VPU execute together?
The host waits for the projection and transfers scaled values.
It clocks one lane to completion before launching the next.
Independent dispatch and two accessible buffers allow overlap.
Wait for scaled data. Reuse a buffer only after the VPU releases it.
